facts.title: Khorovats
facts.text: No Armenian feast without this grilled meat dish, in Armenia as across the diaspora.

facts.title: "Grilled"
facts.text: From the verb khorovel, "to grill", derived from the Indo-European root qor, meaning to burn.

facts.title: The shepherd's barbecue
facts.text: Sewn back into its own skin, the lamb spent the night beneath the embers, like roasted chestnuts.

facts.title: 2 to 12 hours
facts.text: Onions, salt, purple basil or savory, but no vinegar: Armenia rejects it.

facts.title: 12 to 15 cm
facts.text: Between the coals and the shampoors, largest pieces in the center, skewers packed close together.

facts.title: When September Comes
facts.text: Armen Dzhigarkhanyan grills khorovats on a Moscow balcony; the neighbors call the fire department.

facts.title: 15,000 attendees
facts.text: In 2012, they gathered at the annual khorovats festival, around the smoking skewers.

ytTitle: Khorovats, the Armenian art of grilling
ytLead: An iconic dish of Armenian festivities, khorovats embodies a centuries-old art of grilling, blending rituals, history and conviviality. Since 2009, the town of Akhtala has hosted an annual festival in its honor.
